papers.t: Ohmic warm inflation
papers.abs: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.
papers.comment: 34 pages, 3 figures. Webinar presentation: https://youtu.be/7dMY6vakaAo

papers.t: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
papers.abs: The first stars formed out of light elements (H, He, and Li leftover from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis) and began the chemical enrichment of the Universe. Identifying this first-generation population of stars, known as Population III, and understanding their properties is one of the most ambitious goals of modern extragalactic astrophysics. We report the detection of He and H emission lines and extremely low Oxygen abundance in AMORE6, a strongly magnified galaxy at redshift z = 5.725, i.e. approximately one billion years after the Big Bang, with deep James Webb Space Telescope spectroscopy. He II lambda1640 and lambda4686 emission lines are detected at 16.7 sigma and 4.0 sigma significance, respectively. The observed He II-to-Hbeta ratios are consistent with predictions for extreme ionizing radiation fields and the low chemical compositions typical of Population III stars. Oxygen abundance of the interstellar medium is estimated to be 8 x 10^-4 solar from weak [OIII]lambda4363 and lambda5008 lines, consistent with an almost pristine environment, perhaps enriched by the Pop III stars themselves. Although we cannot exclude alternative sources of hard ionizing radiation, such as accreting black holes, these observations offer the first view of the extremely low metallicity environment where the Universe's first stars are predicted to be born. The data show that such pockets of pristine gas still exist one billion years after the Big Bang and that they are dominated by very massive stars.
papers.comment: Submitted

papers.t: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
papers.abs: Buoyancy glitches in red giants provide localized information on the interior structure near the base of the convective envelope, but their properties are typically inferred from dedicated seismic modelling rather than global properties, limiting large-sample applications. We investigate whether the buoyancy-glitch amplitude ($A_g$), location ($W_{\rm g}^{\star}$), and width ($D_g$) can be recovered from global stellar properties using gradient-boosted tree regressors (XGBoost and LightGBM). The models were trained on a grid of 12580 synthetic stellar models of low-luminosity red giants, with target parameters derived from fits to the local buoyancy frequency profile. We find that $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ exhibit excellent recoverability, achieving test-set $\mathcal{R}^2$ values of 0.98 and 0.97, respectively. In contrast, $A_g$ shows moderate recoverability overall ($\mathcal{R}^2=0.68$). This reduced recoverability of $A_g$ is concentrated in the large frequency separation range $Δν= 4.6$--$18.9\,μ$Hz, where the glitch resides in the evanescent-zone transition between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity, increasing intrinsic scatter. SHAP analysis shows that $ν_{\rm max}$ and $T_{\rm eff}$ dominate the predictions across all targets, indicating that the regressors rely primarily on evolutionary state. While $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ are tightly constrained by global evolutionary trends, the lower recoverability of $A_g$ reflects localized structural complexity associated with red-giant evolution. Overall, for the synthetic grid adopted here, these results indicate that global properties provide a direct estimate of the buoyancy-glitch parameters and a way to prioritise dedicated mixed-mode inversions for large asteroseismic samples such as Kepler and PLATO.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 8 figures

papers.t: Atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances of young stars with APOGEE -- II. Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, and Sulphur abundances in Orion
papers.abs: We derived the abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, and iron in young G-, K-, and M-type stars (effective temperatures of 3500--5900 K) using APOGEE-2 infrared spectra. Our final sample comprises 195 slow rotators ($v\sin i$ $\leq$ 30 km~s$^{-1}$) in the Orion complex (Orion A, B, OB1, and $λ$~Ori). The abundances were determined using MARCS model atmospheres, atmospheric parameters derived with \tona, and the \bacc\ code. We obtained median abundances of $ε$(C) = 8.37$\pm$0.10, $ε$(N) = 7.35$\pm$0.16, $ε$(O) = 8.63$\pm$0.08, $ε$(S) = 7.19$\pm$0.18, and $ε$(Fe) = 7.45$\pm$0.05. Nitrogen is subsolar ([N/H] $=-0.48$), whereas carbon, oxygen, sulphur, and iron are within 0.1 dex of the solar values. We find no spatial structure within the Orion subgroups, and the only significant difference is a 0.29 dex lower nitrogen abundance in Orion A than in Orion OB1, which does not extend to the other elements. Compared with 430 nearby main-sequence stars analysed in the same way, Orion shows carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen abundances lower by 0.1--0.2 dex, although consistent within the errors, whereas sulphur and iron differ by less than 0.07 dex. We also compare our abundances with nebular abundances of HII regions and star-forming galaxies: the stellar abundances of oxygen, sulphur, and iron are higher, with the largest offset in iron, although the agreement in abundance ratios improves when temperature inhomogeneities and dust depletion are taken into account.
papers.comment: 22 pages, 6 Figures, 6 Tables. Accepted in MNRAS

papers.t: An early interaction between the Sagittarius dwarf and the Milky Way I: Fossil signatures in the phase-space structure of the disc
papers.abs: Several independent lines of evidence point to an early encounter between the Milky Way and the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy $5$-$7$ Gyr ago. We present four controlled $N$-body+hydro simulations, one of an isolated host galaxy and three of a single interaction between a Milky-Way-like host and a Sagittarius-like satellite on an unbound polar orbit. Relative to the fiducial satellite (with total mass $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$), one run increases the satellite's mass by a factor of $1.5$ and another its crossing speed by a factor of $1.4$, giving pericentric speeds of $466$-$634$ km s$^{-1}$ at pericentric radii of $R\simeq15$-$18$ kpc. Comparing the present-day, phase-space structure in radial bins by age of newly-formed thin-disc stars across the runs, we find that stars that existed at the time of the passage are thickened by up to $\sim37$ per cent in mass-enclosed height and heated by up to $\sim5$ km s$^{-1}$ in vertical velocity dispersion relative to the control, while stars formed after the passage are unaffected. The heating signature is also evident when comparing the age-vertical velocity dispersion relation against a heating relation with a power law of $0.38$, obtained by fitting the isolated host. A single, disc crossing from an early interaction thus suffices to leave lasting, datable fossils in the age-resolved vertical structure of a galactic disc. The fiducial run's dispersion jump of $\sim4$ km s$^{-1}$ matches best with that observed in the outer low-$α$ disc of the Milky Way (Das et al. 2024), corresponding to a perturber mass of $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$, with a velocity of $466$ km s$^{-1}$ at a pericentric radius of $16.7$ kpc, though the inversion from jump amplitude to perturber mass is good only to a factor of $\sim1.5$.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to MNRAS

papers.t: A TESS Search for Optical Variability in Intermediate-mass Black Hole Candidates
papers.abs: Optical variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) probes accretion onto black holes. We study the optical variability of AGNs in the mass range of intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs, $10^{2-6}\,M_\odot$), whose expected variability damping timescales are of order days. We use the high-cadence photometry of the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to search for optical variability within its individual 28-day sectors. By applying the Quaver light-curve reduction pipeline and designing artifact-aware variability metrics, we identify 3 sources with high-confidence variability and 17 sources with medium-confidence variability. Fitting damped random walk (DRW) models reveals a tentative timescale-mass correlation in a small, metric-selected subset, but not in the full sample. ZTF difference-image aperture photometry reveals long-term fractional variability of 1.8-7.4% in the high-confidence sources, while most medium-confidence sources have variability below 1%. This study demonstrates that the dense cadence and repeated full-sky observations of TESS are valuable for detecting IMBH optical variability, while also being limited by its instrumental artifacts and relatively shallow field.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ApJ

papers.t: Hotter than Little Red Dots: Two Quasars with T~10⁴ K blackbody-like continua at z~4
papers.abs: Gas envelope models of Little Red Dots (LRDs) predict a transition from cool ($T\sim5000\,\mathrm{K}$), gas-enshrouded accretion to an exposed quasar, but observational candidates remain scarce. We identify two blackbody quasars (BBQs), JADES1180 at $z=3.711$ and GTO1215 at $z=4.552$, among 3,553 sources with archival NIRSpec/PRISM spectra. Both show extremely red rest-frame UV ($β_\mathrm{UV}>2.0$) but blue optical continua ($β_\mathrm{opt}<-0.75$), where $f_λ\proptoλ^β$. Their $Λ$-shaped UV-optical continua peak at $λ\approx3000-4000$ Å and are not reproduced by a quasar template reddened with an SMC-like extinction curve. Under the gas envelope interpretation, UV-to-mid-infrared spectral energy distribution fitting indicates $T_\mathrm{env}\approx7600-10300\,\mathrm{K}$ and $L_\mathrm{env}\simeq(3-15)\times10^{45}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, placing both sources just above the typical LRD ranges in temperature and luminosity. Both BBQs show hot-dust emission with $T_\mathrm{dust}\simeq1400-1550\,\mathrm{K}$ and X-ray emission with $L_\mathrm{2-10\,keV}\simeq(1.3-4.5)\times10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The gas absorption is $N_\mathrm{H}<1.5\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$, indicating Compton-thin absorption sightlines. Both also exhibit far-infrared and millimeter detections, suggesting an additional cooler dust component, potentially associated with their host galaxies. These properties are consistent with a transitional phase in which a hotter gaseous envelope partially exposes the central engine.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to AAS journal

papers.t: Diffusing the assumptions: towards realistic LISA stochastic component separation with physics-aware simulation-based inference
papers.abs: Simultaneous global-fit inference of the numerous sources observed by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) depends on accurate modeling of its stochastic components: instrumental noise, the Galactic foreground, and astrophysical or stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWB). Realistic features such as non-Gaussian transients and data gaps challenge traditional likelihood-based pipelines, creating an opportunity for simulation-based inference (SBI) to augment traditional analyses. Here, we present an SBI framework for LISA stochastic component separation built on the Simformer, a transformer trained with diffusion or flow matching that ingests the full time-delay interferometry cross-spectral matrix via a physics-aware embedding. We progressively relax standard simplifying assumptions on simulated 11.6-day datasets containing a loud foreground and a faint power-law SGWB. With unequal arms and per-link noise freedom, the networks match 17-dimensional MCMC posteriors after importance reweighting; full cross-spectra constrain each link's optical metrology noise amplitude to $1\%$. When marginalizing over glitches or massive black hole binary transients, estimation errors remain flat up to transient signal-to-noise ratios of several hundred, whereas ignoring them severely biases likelihood fits. Under time-varying spline noise levels, realistic glitch rates, and gaps up to one day long, posterior coverage remains nominal or conservative across $\sim 10^4$ simulations. We test coverage in the local neighborhood of a given observation by introducing a novel importance-weighted localized simulation-based calibration test. We find flow matching slightly better calibrated than diffusion in simpler regimes and observe modest gains from physics-aware template inputs. Finally, we outline how these networks can initialize the noise and stochastic blocks of a LISA global fit.
papers.comment: 38 pages, 15 figures, 2 tables

papers.t: Carving the Neptunian desert as a function of stellar mass and lifetime XUV irradiation
papers.abs: The Neptunian desert is a prominent feature in the exoplanet population, thought to arise from both XUV-driven photoevaporation and tidal circularisation following high-eccentricity migration. However, the extent to which each mechanism contributes, and where, remains uncertain. We examine the desert as a function of stellar type as a test of these mechanisms. We determine the desert boundaries for subsamples of F, G, K, and M-hosted planets for radius against period, semi-major axis, bolometric instellation, and lifetime XUV irradiation. Going from F to M, we observe shifts in the boundary between 2.2-7.5 R$_\oplus$ towards shorter orbital periods, smaller orbital distances, and much smaller instellations. These shifts match changes in lifetime XUV irradiation as a function of stellar mass at fixed period, semi-major axis, and bolometric instellation, evidence towards a photoevaporative origin for the desert at these radii. This is especially the case for orbital period, where the boundary should be invariant across stellar types under the high-eccentricity mechanism. In lifetime XUV space, we see significant overlap in the boundary across stellar types up to 7.5 R$_\oplus$. While this could be further evidence towards the XUV-driven mechanism in this regime, our uncertainties cannot rule out a shift in the boundary of the magnitude expected under the high-eccentricity mechanism. Overall, our results suggest a photoevaporative origin of the Neptunian desert up to sub-Saturn radii, but increased sample sizes, especially for M-hosted, Neptune-sized planets, will help distinguish further between the mechanisms.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables. Accepted for publication in MNRAS

papers.t: What determines the properties of Population III binaries?
papers.abs: Population~III binaries may provide a gravitational-wave probe of the first stellar populations. Uncertain initial binary parameter distributions and evolutionary prescriptions complicate predictions of their remnant masses, birth orbits and formation spins. Varying these model evolutionary parameters (MEPs) jointly is needed to identify which MEPs shape each property and whether their effects persist among binaries that merge. We use \textsc{StarTrack} to evolve $2\times10^6$ initial binaries per model across 1152 configurations spanning eight MEPs. To our knowledge, this is the largest grid of Population~III isolated-binary population-synthesis models to date by number of distinct parameter configurations. We compare the properties and correlations of all binary black holes (BBHs) with those of systems that merge within the adopted age of the Universe. The all-BBH (merging-BBH) model medians span $34.3$--$171.0 M_{\odot}$ ($23.1$--$94.8 M_{\odot}$) in total mass, $0.039$--$0.106$ ($0.018$--$0.129$) in effective aligned spin $χ_{\mathrm{eff}}$ at formation, and $0.075$--$0.639$ ($0.039$--$0.983$) in birth eccentricity. Merger selection also changes correlations between BBH properties and the combinations of MEP values and prescriptions associated with them. We use variance-based sensitivity analysis to quantify how the initial binary parameter distributions and evolutionary prescriptions affect the predicted BBH properties.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 5 figures. Abstract abridged for arxiv

papers.t: Precise Interstellar Extinction Estimates for Nearly Ten Million Stars Based on Multiple Spectroscopic Surveys
papers.abs: Accurate interstellar extinction estimates are vital for revealing the intrinsic physical properties of stars and the dynamic structure of the Milky Way. Based on multiple optical and near-infrared spectroscopic surveys, including LAMOST, APOGEE, GALAH, GaiaESO, SEGUE, and DESI, we use MLPs and polynomial regressions to calibrate giants and dwarfs separately onto the APOGEE parameter scale, constructing a combined spectroscopic catalog of nearly ten million stars with calibrated stellar atmospheric parameters. This catalog not only provides a robust dataset for our extinction measurements, but also serves as a reference sample for estimating stellar parameters from photometric surveys. Both cross-survey comparisons and external comparisons with high-resolution spectroscopic benchmarks show good agreement in the calibrated parameters. By applying the star-pair method to this extensive sample, we obtain precise extinction estimates. Incorporating distance information, we characterize the spatial distribution of extinction covering over 33,000 square degrees of the sky. Comparisons with existing literature demonstrate that our extinction estimates achieve an exceptional precision of 0.019-0.022 mag. The value-added catalog and open-source Python pipeline for line-of-sight extinction released in this work will provide robust support for future Galactic structure studies and photometric calibrations.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics (RAA). 22 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables

papers.t: 2026 QQ8: Earth's temporary flyby of maximum lunation
papers.abs: Aims: On a rare occasion, asteroids are temporarily captured by the Earth to become the planet's interim companions. The discovery of asteroid 2026~QQ$_8$ provided an opportunity to study this class of objects, adding to the sparse discovery catalogue of Earth's temporary companions. Methods: We performed astrometric, photometric, and dynamical studies of 2026~QQ$_8$, and measured its solar radiation pressure signal to discern between a natural and an artificial origin. Results: We find 2026 QQ$_8$ to be of natural origin, with solar radiation pressure signal commensurable with natural objects and spectrophotometry of an S-type object. 2026 QQ$_8$ is Earth's third discovered otemporarily-captured companion on a flyby orbit, and the first long-duration one, owing this to being on the so-called "orbit of maximum lunation". Its unusual orbit lies close to the theoretical upper duration limit of an object captured in the Earth-Moon system, and has now been observed for the first time.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, submitted to A&A

papers.t: TDI-∞ and beyond
papers.abs: Time-delay interferometry (TDI) cancels the laser frequency noise that dominates the measurements of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), and relies on interpolating the laser noise to fractional delays. In TDI-$\infty$, which finds the laser noise free combinations from a linear model of the measurements, the interpolation sets the design matrix, and any interpolation error leaves uncanceled laser noise which is not accounted for. We introduce Gaussian process (GP) interpolation into TDI-$\infty$, which models the laser noise from its spectrum and propagates its interpolation error into the likelihood as a covariance. We test it on a realistic data model in which the measurements pass through the on-board anti-alias filter and are downsampled to the 4 Hz telemetry rate, either applying the filter after the delays, as on the spacecraft, or building the filter into the GP kernel. We compare it with Lagrange and cosine-sum interpolation, and also keep the column space of the design matrix, which the standard null space likelihood discards. In lisainstrument simulations all three interpolators cancel the laser noise for a 1 Hz filter band edge, but only the GP does so up to the 2 Hz Nyquist frequency, a range the Lagrange and cosine-sum interpolators were not designed for. In parameter estimation on 200 simulated galactic binaries, the GP with the filter in its kernel gives the smallest calibrated posteriors. The differences are small for a single long data segment and grow when the data are split into short chunks or contain gaps, where the column space also recovers some information, by an amount that depends on the threshold that defines the null space.

papers.t: The Time Domain Telescope: A Global Spectroscopic Array
papers.abs: The Time Domain Telescope (TDT) is an initiative in the context of the ESO Expanding Horizons program. The TDT project aims for a global telescope array for spectroscopic time-resolved and time-critical observations in the optical-near-infrared, with a core at the European Southern Observatory and partners around the world. The TDT core consists of 100 unit telescopes of 2-meter diameter each that are fully Adaptive Optics-assisted in the blue, to deliver an enclosed energy of >=80% within 0.12" at 400nm. The unit telescopes are coupled to a set of spectrographs covering spectral resolutions R=10^3 - 10^5 over the wavelength range 0.35 - 1.8 micrometer. The combination of extreme adaptive optics with near-read-noise-free detectors will allow the TDT to reach unprecedented depths and/or high cadence. When all 100 units target a single object a depth of 25 mag can be reached in 30 minutes at a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 per spectral resolution element at a spectral resolution of R=5000. With this the TDT will spectroscopically match the imaging depth of the Vera Rubin Observatory and the Euclid and Roman spacecrafts, the expected brightness of electromagnetic counterparts discovered by the LISA space mission, as well as by the next-generation gravitational wave detectors. The science of the TDT covers a large part of astronomy, and ranges from the outer Solar System, to stellar and binary systems to extragalactic transients and the growth of supermassive black holes, all the way back to the expansion history of the Universe. The TDT is transformational, unique and highly complementary to the current and near-future ESO facilities, in particular by providing the possibility for time-resolved spectroscopic observations well below the brightness of the optical night sky.
papers.comment: 20 pages, contribution to the IAU Symposium 406 'Future Landscape of Astrophysical Transients'

papers.t: Disrupted stars and captured compact objects: Combining observations from multiple messengers to infer the population of massive black holes
papers.abs: Massive black holes (MBHs) are found in galactic centres, but their formation and evolution remain elusive. Tidal disruption events (TDEs) and extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) both arise from stellar dynamics in the nuclear star clusters around MBHs, and are observed with electromagnetic surveys and gravitational waves, respectively. To overcome the scarcity of coincident detections, we formulate how to combine gravitational-wave detections from LISA-EMRIs with observations from ZTF-TDEs to measure properties of the MBH population. Building on two-dimensional Fokker-Planck simulations of EMRIs and TDEs, we model how their populations are affected by the MBH-host scaling relation, the nucleation fraction and the MBH occupation fraction, and analyse the resulting catalogues using joint hierarchical inference accounting for their individual selection biases. With current ZTF-TDE detections, we can already identify combinations of MBH formation favoured by and consistent with the observed TDE population, and derive corresponding predictions for the EMRI population detectable by LISA. Across a range of astrophysical assumptions, the ratio of detectable TDEs to EMRIs is high: ZTF detecting 2.7-84.3 times as many TDEs as LISA detects EMRIs. TDEs, through their numbers, set the shared mass and redshift distributions: LSST constrains the characteristic MBH mass to a 90% credible width of 0.31 dex and the power-law index of the redshift evolution to a precision of 0.11. EMRIs make up ~3.4% of the joint catalogue, yet carry more information than the whole ZTF sample and are the only probe of MBH spin and orbital eccentricity. TDEs will constrain the abundance of low-mass MBHs before LISA flies, while EMRIs will measure properties that electromagnetic surveys cannot. EMRI and TDE observations offer complementary insights into MBH growth and evolution that neither can provide alone.
papers.comment: 21 pages. Submitted to MNRAS, 19 figures

papers.t: Probing for relativistic outflows in the Ultraluminous X-ray pulsar RX J0209.6-7427
papers.abs: Context. Relativistic winds have been observed in Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs), but their detection at large distances remains limited. Galactic neutron stars accreting matter from Be-star companions provide a valuable opportunity to improve our understanding of these outflows. Aims. RX J0209.6-7427 is a Be-XRB, powered by a neutron star with a spin period of 9.3 seconds, that underwent an outburst in 2019, exceeding a bolometric luminosity of $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$ at its peak. Owing to its relatively low distance and a high-resolution XMM-Newton observation, this source is a strong candidate for investigating outflows associated with super-Eddington accretion. Methods. The RGS spectrum yields 105,000 counts, a factor of two higher than any other deep ULX RGS spectrum. RGS and EPIC-pn data sets were modelled with a phenomenological continuum accounting for emission from the accretion disc and accretion column. The emission and absorption features were fitted with the optically-thin plasma models available in SPEX, exploring the temperature-velocity parameter space. Results. The modelling of emission features suggests the presence of a multiphase photoionised plasma approximately at rest with respect to the source. The absorption features can be reproduced either by blueshifted photoionised absorbers moving at approximately $0.1c$ and $0.2c$, the latter being more tentative, or by an alternative collisionally ionised absorption model, which provides a comparably acceptable fit. The presence of ultrafast outflows therefore remains a plausible, but non-unique, interpretation of the data. If associated with outflows, the inferred column densities appear lower than those reported for some persistent ULXs, potentially reflecting differences in the accretion-flow properties or the shorter super-Eddington phase of RX J0209.6-7427.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 14 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics

papers.t: Characterisation of B-type stars in four young Galactic open clusters. II. Photometric variability with TESS and identification of pulsating stars
papers.abs: Pulsations and binarity are important properties of massive stars and influence their structure and evolution. Young open clusters are ideal laboratories to study massive stars, since they are mostly coeval and chemically homogeneous. We analyse 82 B-type stars in the Galactic open clusters $h$ and $χ$ Persei, NGC 457, NGC 581, and NGC 1960, which have ages between 15 and 30 Myr. We extract light curves using both simple aperture photometry and a point-spread-function-based method that minimises contamination from crowded fields in full-frame images from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. We successfully extract light curves for 63 stars. The majority have photometric variability caused by pulsations, showing how pulsations are a common property of young B-type stars in clusters. We classify stars into different pulsator types based on their spectral type and frequency spectrum. The most common pulsator class are beta Cephei stars, with 29 stars in total, and we discover pulsation modes in almost all stars with a spectral type of B2 or earlier. All Be stars show pulsations, which supports the consensus of the ubiquity of pulsations in these stars. Finally, we confirm that the majority of early B-type stars are in binary systems, except for two pulsating Be stars and a star with rotational modulation. This indicates that pulsations do not significantly bias the spectroscopic detection of short-period binaries, except for Be stars where the spectroscopic radial velocity variability threshold should be higher than the typical value of 20 km s$^{-1}$.

papers.t: PHOTO-CAT - Photometric Contamination Analyzer Tool: A High-Performance Framework for Photometric Contamination Assessment
papers.abs: High-precision photometric missions are sensitive to flux contamination from neighboring stars, which can bias light curves, dilute transit depths, and compromise photometric precision. We present PHOTO-CAT, a catalog-driven, mission-agnostic tool for quantifying stellar flux contamination in photometric observations. The tool builds a three-dimensional Euclidean representation of the sky from a user-provided astrometric catalog, indexes it with a memory-optimized KDTree for rapid neighbor searches, and computes per-target contamination metrics from angular separation, relative fluxes, and configurable aperture models (top-hat or circular Gaussian PSF), optionally converted into an arbitrary instrumental bandpass via empirical photometric relations or stellar spectral models. A streaming, CSR-style storage format with compact internal identifiers enables scalable processing of catalogs with tens to hundreds of millions of sources with minimal memory overhead. Outputs include per-target contaminating flux, contamination ratios, target purity, number of neighboring sources, and their angular separations, supporting target screening and field-selection decisions ahead of observations. We demonstrate the software performance on all-sky Gaia samples (G <= 12, with neighbors down to G = 17; over three million targets), providing global contamination statistics and spatial characterization of crowded regions, and apply it to the Ariel Mission Candidate Sample to show how wavelength-dependent contamination estimates support target selection and observing-geometry optimization. Although developed for the Mauve satellite, PHOTO-CAT is mission-agnostic and readily applicable to TESS, PLATO, Ariel, and other surveys.
papers.comment: Article accepted for pubblication by RASTI with official acceptance date 20/11/2026

papers.t: Nuclear Precision and Multimessenger Constraints on Neutron-Star Structure
papers.abs: Neutron-star cores retain structural freedom beyond the constraints supplied by nuclear measurements. We quantify this freedom through an observable-dependent variance ceiling and identify radius--Love compensation as a mechanism suppressing nuclear constraints on tides. Across four data-conditioned equation-of-state families, a pulsar radius measured to 0.3 km paired with a binary tide measured to 10\% removes 44--68\% of the current logarithmic Love-number variance. The framework connects laboratory precision and complementary stellar measurements to core structure.
papers.comment: 26 Pages, 7 Figures

papers.t: Coronagraphic time-delay interferometry: fundamental steps towards concrete applications
papers.abs: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a future space-based gravitational wave (GW) observatory. Central to LISA data analysis is time-delay interferometry (TDI), which reduces otherwise overwhelming laser frequency noise. In previous work, we explored coronagraphic TDI, a sky-dependent null-stream channel which cancels the GW signal of a point-like source when pointed at its sky position. Because this property relies only on the geometric response of LISA, coronagraphic TDI is a candidate for model-agnostic sky localization. Here, we address three challenges which arise when analyzing realistic LISA data: (i) spacecraft motion; (ii) signal superposition; (iii) instrumental noise. We derive a second-generation coronagraphic TDI variable and its analytic noise model, and show that it reduces laser frequency noise in the presence of spacecraft motion while still recovering the position of the source. Using pairs of Galactic binaries (GBs), we find that sources can be localized independently provided they do not overlap in frequency, even when they share the same sky position, whereas sources overlapping in frequency can only be localized if one dominates by a factor of ~100 in amplitude. This is confirmed by the analysis of a simulation containing a massive black hole binary and 49 verification GBs. Finally, we introduce a statistical test based on the analytic noise model, which provides well-calibrated confidence regions for the sky position of the source. Applying it to GBs in the presence of instrumental noise, we find that the geometric response alone only weakly constrains the sky position: even at signal-to-noise ratios of order 10^4, 90% confidence regions span ~10^3 deg^2. These are fundamental steps towards applications of coronagraphic TDI to LISA data, such as sky localization and glitch discrimination, which we discuss.

papers.t: Hints of planet formation in progress around DR Tau from observations with LBT SHARK-NIR and SHARK-VIS
papers.abs: Protoplanetary disks are the primary sites of planet formation. However, the direct imaging of protoplanets still embedded within their parental disks remains a significant challenge, with only a small number of confirmed detections to date and several candidates awaiting verification. We search for embedded planets in the protoplanetary disk of the young star DRTau by targeting accretion signatures from forming sub-stellar objects. Using narrow-band imaging, we observe both visible Halpha and near-infrared Paschen-beta (Pabeta) emission to identify actively accreting companions. To this end, we performed high-contrast observations of DRTau using the SHARK-VIS (0.40-0.95 micron) and SHARK-NIR (0.96-1.70 micron) imagers at the LBT. The study uses a combination of narrow-band filters to isolate accretion signatures and broad-band filters for multi-wavelength characterization in both the visible and near-infrared. Our observations recover the primary disk structures previously identified in the literature, albeit at low signal-to-noise (S/N). We identify two compact features with S/N between 6 and 13 in both narrow- and broad-band filters. The first, an elongated structure, matches previous SPHERE detections, while the second, more compact feature, is now confirmed despite its low S/N in earlier datasets. A comparison over a seven-year baseline confirms the stability of both structures. Their observed orbital motion is consistent with Keplerian rotation, potentially suggesting the presence of an undetected planetary-mass companion (few MJup) at the location of the second feature. However, our analysis does not confirm Halpha or Pabeta emission originating from localized accretion. Instead, we conclude that the observed flux is likely stellar light reflected by dust at these locations and discuss alternative mechanisms that could account for such detections.
papers.comment: 12 pages; 10 Figures; Accepted for publications on A&A

papers.t: Nuclear Urca cooling in magnetar crust and anomalous heating
papers.abs: We present a new result that the nuclear Urca process in magnetars, associated with ultrastrong magnetic field, dramatically alters the neutrino cooling efficiency to support higher surface temper ature, which is not common in ordinary neutron stars. A new formalism for neutrino luminosity accommodating finite temperature on top of magnetic field is extended with the use of realistic nuclear structure inputs for the Urca pair 29Na-29Mg. We find that the neutrino luminosity of Urca pair shows a spiral variation as a function of magnetic field and crust density, while the Urca pair persists, in contrast to previous studies. Applying geometrically correct volumetric energy loss rate to Urca shell at fixed density with varying magnetic field strength, our results show that thermally populated excited states at finite temperature enhance neutrino luminosity, whereas conditions con strained Urca-pair formation driven by ultrastrong magnetic field reduce cooling efficiency, which can explain high temperature of magnetar surface as a new possibility.

papers.t: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
papers.abs: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 2 figures

papers.t: The GAPS programme at TNG. LXXXIII. Orbital refinement and atmospheric investigation of TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b)
papers.abs: TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b) is a highly irradiated ultra-hot Jupiter on a strongly misaligned orbit, a benchmark target for atmospheric and dynamical studies. We comprehensively characterise the TOI-1518 system by refining its orbital and physical parameters, and by investigating the chemical composition of the planetary atmosphere through transmission spectroscopy. We employed a joint Bayesian framework combining TESS photometry, HARPS-N high-resolution spectroscopy, and least-squares deconvolution profiles to break stellar geometrical degeneracies. We then applied single-line and cross-correlation function (CCF) transmission spectroscopy across theoretical templates. By anchoring the stellar projected rotational velocity ($v \sin i_\star \approx 79.7$ km s$^{-1}$), we confirmed the nearly polar orbit ($λ\approx 238^\circ$) and the theoretically predicted nodal precession ($\mathrm{d}i/\mathrm{d}t \approx 0.15^\circ$ yr$^{-1}$). We revealed an atmospheric Rossiter-McLaughlin (RM) effect and a bulk atmospheric blue-shift of $\approx -7.0$ km s$^{-1}$. Through transmission spectroscopy, we detected H I, C I, Na I, Ca I, Sc II, Ti II, V II, Cr I, Fe I, Fe II, Ni I, Sr II, Y II, Eu II, and W I. This marks the first detection of H I, C I, Sc II, V II, Sr II, Y II, Eu II, and W I in this planet, and the first ever detection of Eu II and W I in an exoplanetary atmosphere. Inconsistencies in the Na I doublet shifts suggest likely stellar contamination. Furthermore, time-resolved CCF analysis revealed morning-to-evening limb asymmetries for species like Mg I and Ba I, hinting at night-side cold traps. The atmosphere of TOI-1518 b exhibits a rich chemical inventory shaped by intense irradiation and bulk circulation. Our results emphasize the necessity of simultaneously modelling stellar line morphology and planetary tracks to accurately interpret atmospheric signals under strong RM effects.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)

papers.t: WISDOM Project -- XXIX. Catalogue of CO observations of nearby galaxies and the CO Tully-Fisher relation
papers.abs: We present Tully-Fisher relations (TFRs) that use carbon monoxide (CO) as the kinematic tracer and Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) $W1$-band and Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS) $K_\text{s}$-band magnitudes as tracers of stellar luminosity. CO data were obtained using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array for the mm-Wave Interferometric Survey of Dark Object Masses (WISDOM) project for a sample of $102$ galaxies located at redshifts $z \lesssim 0.03$, with $81$ detections. The best-fitting reverse $W1$-band and $K_\text{s}$-band CO TFRs are $M_{W1}=(-7.18\pm0.93)\left[\log\left(\frac{W_{50}/\sin i}{\text{km~s}^{-1}}\right)-2.6\right]+(-24.04\pm0.13)$ and $M_{K_\text{s}}=(-5.95\pm0.62)\left[\log\left(\frac{W_{50}/\sin i}{\text{km~s}^{-1}}\right)-2.6\right]+(-24.01\pm0.10)$, respectively, where $W_{50}$ is the velocity width of each integrated CO spectrum at $50\%$ of its maximum, $i$ is the galaxy inclination and $M$ is the galaxy absolute magnitude. Our results are in excellent agreement with those of Tiley et al. (2016b), and together they constitute a robust local benchmark for the CO TFR. We however measure a shallower slope and a smaller zero-point offset compared to the relation of Tully & Pierce (2000). Due to the morphological diversity of our sample, we construct separate late-type and early-type galaxy (ETG) CO TFRs, finding that ETGs are $1.40\pm0.39$~mag fainter at $W1$ band and $0.89\pm0.28$~mag fainter at $K_\text{s}$ band at a given velocity width. We also generate and include a comprehensive catalogue of WISDOM CO data products for use in future molecular gas studies.
papers.comment: 60 pages, 5 figures, accepted by MNRAS

papers.t: Blowing star formation away in AGN Hosts (BAH) - VI. Warm Molecular Outflows Driven by the Low-Luminosity AGN in NGC 3884
papers.abs: We use the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) Medium Resolution Spectrograph (MRS) to investigate the warm molecular and low ionization gas outflows driven by the low-luminosity Active Galactic Nucleus (AGN) in NGC 3884. By decomposing the emission-line profiles into multiple Gaussian components, we detect both ionized and warm molecular outflows, traced by [Ar ii] 6.99 um and H2 0-0 S(5), respectively. The ionized and warm molecular components both extend to similar distances from the nucleus, reaching approximately ~1.2 kpc. In addition to an outflow component, we detect a double narrow emission component in both ionized and molecular lines, clearly observed along the minor axis with similar amplitudes, while their intensity ratio varies systematically along the major axis. Both components exhibit similar line widths and centroid velocity distributions, indicating that they are not associated with outflows, but instead arise from gas in the galaxy disk. We estimate that the outflow injects momentum into the interstellar medium (ISM) at a rate corresponding to ~0.015 percent of the AGN bolometric luminosity, consistent with a radiation-driven origin. Assuming a constant outflow rate, the gas reservoir would be depleted on a timescale of ~26 Myr, potentially suppressing nuclear star formation in the host galaxy.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication by AAS

papers.t: Modelling scintillation in Fast Radio Bursts
papers.abs: Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are bright, ms-duration, extragalactic radio transients. Propagation through inhomogeneities in the ionised medium produces scintillation, observed as frequency-dependent intensity variations in their spectra, with bright patches, called scintles. The characteristic scintillation bandwidth probes scattering material along the line of sight. Measuring this scale can be challenging when the observing bandwidth of the burst spectra contains a few scintles. We study the uncertainties associated with recovering $ν_s$ from frequency autocorrelation functions (ACFs) under finite-bandwidth conditions. We examine the recovery of $ν_s$ from individual ACFs and investigate if averaging multiple independent ACFs provides a more robust measurement. Using simulations, we reproduce observational conditions to investigate the modelling of scintillation in ACFs and the associated measurement uncertainties. We use these simulations to test the finite scintle error (FSE) prescription and assess its applicability to real observations. We test the resulting modelling framework on Effelsberg Ultra Broad Band receiver observations of the repeating FRB 20240114A. As the number of scintles decreases, individual ACFs develop fluctuations that deviate from the expected Lorentzian profile. This results in increased scatter in the recovered $ν_s$ and a less reliable FSE prescription. Averaging multiple independent ACFs mitigates these effects and improves the recovery of $ν_s$ in the low-scintle regime. Our results provide a framework for ACF modelling and uncertainty estimation in FRBs. For individual bursts, the FSE is effective with sufficient scintles; we find $η= 0.055$ more suitable for FRB analysis and update the FSE accordingly. For repeaters, averaging multiple ACFs and bootstrap resampling improve the recovery and uncertainty estimation of $ν_s$.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 11 figures, accepted for publication in A&A

papers.t: The First Adolescent Super-Earth-Sized Multi-Planet System Around an M Dwarf: TOI-2079
papers.abs: We identify two planets in close-in orbits around the M-type star TOI-2079 as the first super-Earth-sized planets orbiting a multi-planet M dwarf with a well-determined age of $1$-$2$\,Gyr. The interior planet, TOI-2079 b, has an orbital period of $1.49232359^{+0.00000099}_{-0.00000086}$ d, and the outer planet, TOI-2079 c, has an orbital period of $9.3174523\pm0.0000098$ d. The host star characterization is based on spectroscopic observations, which classify it from an M1.5 to an M3.5 dwarf with an effective temperature of $3695\pm77$ K. Further analysis determined TOI-2079's rotation period to be $17.33^{+0.29}_{-0.28}$ d. Multiple ground-based follow-up observations, combined with a state-of-the-art validation procedure, allow us to rule out possible astrophysical false-positive scenarios and validate the planetary nature of both objects. We find that the inner planet has a radius of $1.320\pm0.050 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 867\pm27$ K, while the outer planet has $R_{\rm p} = 1.671\pm0.051 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 473\pm15$ K.
papers.comment: 22 pages, 15 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in ApJL

papers.t: Hard X-ray spectroscopy of a short-period asynchronous polar: IGR J19552+0044
papers.abs: IGR J19552+0044 is an asynchronous polar with a beat modulation of $\approx2$ days due to $\approx3$% spin-orbit asynchronism. We present the first hard X-ray properties of this system using a NuSTAR observation. Spectral modeling yields a shock temperature of $kT_{\rm s}=44.50^{+3.60}_{-3.29}$ keV, implying a white dwarf mass of $M_{\rm WD}\geq 0.85\,M_\odot$. We infer an average accretion rate of $\dot{M}\sim 3.0\times 10^{-11}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, consistent with expectations for short-period systems (orbital period $<2$ h). Even at this low accretion rate, we detect a significant Compton reflection component that gives a shock height of $H\sim 0.3\,R_{\rm WD}$. Time-resolved spectroscopy of the observation, covering $\approx61$% of a beat cycle, reveals a variation in $\dot{M}$ by a factor of $\sim 4.5$, providing X-ray evidence for the magnetic valve mechanism. Despite the large variations in $\dot{M}$, no significant change in shock temperature is observed. This weak thermal response constrains the shock structure on the white dwarf surface, favoring a shock height that remains approximately constant as $\dot{M}$ changes, potentially due to variations in the fractional accretion area $f$.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.t: A Relativistic Newton's Third Law for Binaries in Environments
papers.abs: We derive the relativistic form of Newton's Third Law governing the interaction between intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and surrounding relativistic matter fields. Working within a two-parameter expansion, we rewrite the evolution of the secondary's orbital elements in a form resembling the integrated forces acting on the environment, avoiding the need to calculate any gravitational perturbations sourced by the dynamical matter content. Using the retarded and advanced Green's functions, we obtain both instantaneous and orbit-averaged laws relating the rate of change of the secondary's orbital energy and angular momentum to that of the matter and the gravitational-wave fluxes at that order. Our results clarify and correct the mixture of ad hoc balance prescriptions currently employed in the literature, providing first-principles forcing functions for the secondary's orbital elements in two ready-to-use forms: a leading-order formulation suitable for fast evaluation with complex relativistic matter simulations, and a first-post-adiabatic formulation of the energy and angular-momentum evolution in environments that are stationary and axisymmetric at leading order.
papers.comment: 28 pages, 2 figures, 1 stave

papers.t: Ultra-diffuse Galaxies in the Kilo-Degree Survey: Globular Cluster Systems in Cluster and Field Environments
papers.abs: Ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) are extreme low-surface-brightness systems whose formation pathways remain debated. Globular clusters (GCs) can trace their early assembly, but wide-area studies of UDG GC populations remain scarce. We study GC systems of 545 high-quality UDG candidates identified in the Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS) with UDGnet, using a dedicated GC-detection pipeline. We identify 24 UDGs with $N_{\rm GC} \geq 3$ (14 associated with groups or clusters and 10 in the field), and use the globular cluster luminosity function to estimate their distances and physical sizes. At fixed luminosity or stellar mass, group- and cluster-associated UDGs tend to have higher GC counts and specific frequencies than field UDGs, although the distributions overlap substantially. Most systems with $S_N \gtrsim 40$ reside in groups or clusters, while field UDGs generally occupy the lower part of the distribution. Group- and cluster-associated UDGs also more often lie near the upper envelope of the $N_{\rm GC}$--$M_\star$ relation. Empirical GC--halo mass relations consequently imply higher halo masses at fixed stellar mass and lower stellar-to-halo mass ratios, although this environmental trend is mild. These findings are consistent with efficient early GC formation followed by suppressed or prematurely quenched field-star formation, suggesting that GC-rich UDGs may represent an extension of the dwarf-galaxy population. The environmental trends may reflect differences in early assembly, quenching, infall, and survival histories rather than a sharp field--cluster dichotomy.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 9 figures

papers.t: Predicting HCN, HCO⁺, multi-transition CO, and dust emission of star-forming galaxies
papers.abs: We present an analytical model of a turbulent clumpy star-forming disk that reproduces the spatially resolved observations for 6 molecular lines and 3 continuum bands at 250-700~GHz in the central 30~pc of the Circinus Galaxy. Using the properties of the stellar disk as input, and when matched to the line and continuum emission, the model yields the Toomre $Q$ parameter, mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$, metallicity $Z$, and cosmic ray ionization rate $ζ_{CR}$. These in turn are used to infer the gas properties (surface density, velocity dispersion, and radial velocity) as well as the star formation rate. Our main findings from the model include a low CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor that varies with radius in the range $α_{\rm CO}=0.5$--1.5 $M_{\odot}$pc$^{-2}/({\rm K\,km\,s}^{-1})$, close to the canonical value for such environments. It shows that CO(3-2) is a poor tracer of the gas mass surface density $Σ_{{\rm H}_2}$ on these small scales, which is better represented by molecules such as HCO$^+$(3-2) with higher critical density. The steep relation between $Σ_{{\rm H}_2}$ and star formation rate surface density $\dotΣ_*$ is typical of compact starburst systems, and the star formation rate (10~$M_{\odot}$kpc$^{-2}$yr$^{-1}$ averaged over the disk) is high enough to drive a wind. Despite this, and in contrast to typical large scale galactic disks, the energy injection rate into the ISM is dominated by gas inflow through the disk rather than the supernova rate. As such, the decreasing inflow rate at smaller radii could be caused by a wind, or indicate a recent increase of the mass inflow from larger scales. We suggest that such variations in the inflow rate could be associated with the nested spiral structures which have been observed in Circinus.
papers.comment: accepted for publication by A&A

papers.t: Obliquity of Mercury with a fluid core and a deformable mantle
papers.abs: In anticipation of BepiColombo's orbital insertion in 2026, this study revisits the rotation of Mercury, modelling it with a fluid core and a deformable mantle. For this well-established physical model, we provide an analytical solution based on a novel Lagrangian formalism. Our approach enables a comprehensive 3D solution for the mantle's orientation, including the phase in longitude at the perihelion. The model incorporates dissipative torques from core-mantle boundary friction and tidal deformations, conservative pressure torques, and the effect of the planet's apsidal precession. We validate the equilibrium positions obtained numerically in previous studies, but identify discrepancies in earlier analytical works. These inconsistencies overestimated the out-of-Cassini-plane offset induced by tidal deformation by a factor of 100. Additionally, we explore the parameter space to determine where the spin axis deviates most from the Cassini plane and identify a region exhibiting bifurcation in the spin axis equilibrium position. This region cannot be adequately analysed using a model linearised with respect to the obliquity angle.
papers.comment: 9 pages with 5 figures

papers.t: Characterising stellar photometry with invertible neural networks: Joint inference of stellar parameters and extinction
papers.abs: We introduce an extension to a simulation-based deep-learning approach for the characterisation of stellar photometry and investigate the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar properties and extinction. We used the PARSEC stellar evolutionary models to train a conditional invertible neural network (cINN) to jointly estimate full posterior distributions of stellar parameters and extinction. We tested our cINN on synthetic data and real Gaia+2MASS photometry of the two star-forming regions Taurus and Upper Scorpius. We compared our predicted extinction maps to two independent catalogues based on Gaia XP-spectra. On synthetic test data, our trained cINN exhibited a good predictive performance, achieving root mean squared errors (RMSEs) for the maximum a posteriori point estimates of about 0.16 mag for $A_V$, 0.07 dex for $\log(T_{eff}/K)$, 0.16 dex for $\log(g/cms^{-2})$, 0.2 dex for $\log(L/L\odot)$ and 0.1 dex for $\log(M_{ini}/M_\odot)$. Only $\log(age/yr)$ has proven harder to constrain with an RMSE of 0.56 dex. On the Gaia+2MASS observations of Taurus and Upper Scorpius, we retrieved reasonable extinction maps, exhibiting structures that are visually consistent with local clouds. Compared to the independent XP-spectra-based extinction studies, we found a good qualitative agreement and recovered the same prominent spatial structures. Quantitatively, however, we identified an average systematic overestimation of extinction in our approach of 0.5-0.7 mag compared to the spectroscopic studies. We investigated these offsets and identified photometric and distance uncertainties, which are currently unaccounted for in our approach, as likely causes. In conclusion, we demonstrated the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar parameters and extinction with our cINN approach, making it a promising avenue to further pursue for robust and efficient analysis of large photometric surveys.
papers.comment: 27 pages, 14 figures, 1 table, submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics

papers.t: Interstellar extinction estimates for nearly 90 million stars based on synthetic photometry from Gaia XP spectra
papers.abs: Accurate stellar extinction measurements are essential for recovering intrinsic stellar properties and investigating the three-dimensional distribution of interstellar dust. We present reddening estimates for 87,270,425 stars using synthetic SMSS gri photometry derived from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra, combined with Gaia BP and RP, 2MASS JHKs, and WISE W1 photometry. Stellar extinction is determined through empirical SED fitting based on reference stellar loci constructed separately for dwarfs and giants. Comparisons with three external extinction catalogs show good overall agreement, with dispersions of 0.049-0.075 mag in E(B-V). The catalog covers approximately 99.99% of the sky. Using stars with sigma_d/d < 0.2, we further construct reddening maps in four distance ranges from 0 to 5 kpc, revealing prominent molecular clouds and large-scale Galactic dust structures. Extinction-corrected color-absolute-magnitude diagrams show significantly tighter stellar sequences and consistent red-clump features in different Galactic fields. The resulting catalog provides a homogeneous data set for stellar extinction correction and studies of Galactic dust structure.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in New Astronomy. 11 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables

papers.t: Features investigated: A detailed study of axion monodromy inflation using CLiENT
papers.abs: We investigate features in the primordial power spectrum from inflation, specifically those predicted by the axion monodromy model, using recent observational data. In order to compute posteriors, profile likelihoods and Bayesian evidence accurately for the complex likelihood surfaces arising in this model we have used the CLiENT emulator framework. As our data combinations we use both a "conservative" set consisting of Planck PR4 temperature, polarisation and lensing data together with DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more "aggressive" set which also includes small-scale CMB data from ACT and SPT. We find no robust oscillatory feature in current data. With the conservative data the best fit lies at a frequency $ω\simeq 51$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 10.1 relative to a featureless spectrum. However, this feature is disfavoured by the more aggressive data combination, whose best fit lies at $ω\simeq 31$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 7.4. Fits to featureless data are known to give similar improvements, and the Akaike information criterion, the Bayes factors and the look-elsewhere effect all indicate that neither improvement is significant. The amplitude is limited to $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.056$ and $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.062$ (95%) for the two datasets. The emulators reproduce the true log-likelihood at samples of their posteriors with rms errors of 0.07 and 0.16, and the profile likelihoods are calculated with the true likelihood, using the profile capability of CLiENT.
papers.comment: 40 pages, 6 figures, 11 tables

papers.t: Revisiting the Double Cluster in Perseus: Are NGC 869 and NGC 884 a true binary system?
papers.abs: We perform a comprehensive study of the Double Cluster in Perseus, NGC 869 and NGC 884, to investigate their nature and evolutionary state. By combining new CCD $UBV(RI)_{KC}$ photometry with high-precision astrometry and photometry from \textit{Gaia} DR3, we determine robust astrophysical parameters, including colour excess, distance, and age. Our analysis confirms that both clusters are young, with an age of $12\pm1$ Myr, and share similar photometric distances of $2.29$ kpc. By integrating these observational constraints with completeness-corrected mass estimates and a suite of N-body simulations, we examine the kinematic and phase-space properties of the system. We find that the internal kinematics of NGC 884 exhibit a stronger and more coherent expansion signature than NGC 869. Our dynamical simulations demonstrate a rapid increase in the separation of the pair during the first 100 Myr, exceeding $1$ kpc. These results indicate that the system is not currently gravitationally bound and does not constitute a binary cluster. Instead, the Double Cluster is presently unbound, and the forward integrations predict that its components will continue to diverge under the influence of their relative motion and the Galactic potential.
papers.comment: 17 figures, 6 tables. Accepted for publication in MNRAS

papers.t: Baryon-Enhanced Strong Lensing Signatures of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Subhalos
papers.abs: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) is generally expected to suppress subhalo strong lensing through core formation, with subsequent gravothermal collapse potentially enhancing it. We show that compact stars can make a viable population of galaxy-hosting SIDM subhalos more efficient lenses than their cold dark matter (CDM) counterparts. When the baryonic potential weakens or reverses the inner velocity-dispersion gradient, SIDM halos suppress or bypass core formation, allowing inner densities to grow from early times. The evolved SIDM subhalos produce larger deflection angles and tangential caustics than in CDM. Such galaxy-hosting subhalos also dominate the galaxy-galaxy strong-lensing (GGSL) budget in clusters, yet lie far below the resolution of cosmological simulations. We calibrate a baryonic parametric SIDM model to predict their effects in the three most massive TNG300-1 clusters, finding GGSL cross sections 1.4--2.7 times those in CDM, comparable to the excess inferred in recent analyses. Baryon-enhanced SIDM lensing can thus account for the observed GGSL excess and predicts stronger perturbations from luminous satellites, testable through resolved distortions of background arcs and rings.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 9 figures. Model code publicly available at https://github.com/MeiwenYang/BaryonicPSIDM

papers.t: Accurately Measuring Variability Properties from Noisy Light Curves
papers.abs: Modern time-domain surveys probe optical variability near photometric error, challenging weak-signal recovery. The structure function (SF) is widely used for characterizing variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs), but its statistical recovery limits are unclear. Using simulated light curves with realistic errors, we compare three SF estimators from the literature: two non-parametric (pairwise noise subtraction and Bayesian) and one parametric. All recover intrinsic SF when variability dominates, but diverge in the weak regime. The pairwise noise-subtraction estimator approaches an artificial floor when negative variance estimates are discarded, with the floor set by photometric precision and sampling rather than intrinsic variability. The parametric method suffers degeneracy, while the Bayesian estimator yields nearly unbiased SF estimates given well-calibrated photometric errors and adequate sampling. We also derive an idealized detection threshold linking intrinsic variability, photometric precision, and pair counts, providing a reference for assessing the detectability of weak signals. Our results establish statistical limits for SF measurements in the weak-variability regime and offer a framework for accurately measuring low-amplitude variability in AGNs (e.g., extremely stable quasars) and in new populations such as little red dots discovered by JWST.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal; Comments are welcome!

papers.t: Dark Energy Based on Modified Gravity: Where the Future Lies?
papers.abs: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. Since then, many scenarios compatible with the DESI data have been proposed. In particular, there exist several realistic models in the framework of $F(R)$ gravity. In this paper, we show that such realistic models of $F(R)$ gravity may produce an anti-gravity or ghost graviton in the future. The problem could be avoided by further changing the parameters and fine-tuning the initial conditions, but we propose to introduce a potential barrier of the scalar field for the small scalar curvature region, which prevents the Universe from evolving into the anti-gravity or having a ghost graviton region, without the fine-tuning of the initial conditions. We also discuss how this regime can be tested using peculiar velocity and kSZ effect probes.
papers.comment: LaTeX, 25 pages

papers.t: Fast and accurate large-volume Lyman-α forest mocks with three-dimensional U-Net trained on IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO
papers.abs: The Lyman-$α$ forest probes matter structure at $z\gtrsim2$, constraining baryon acoustic oscillations, neutrino masses, and dark matter properties. Interpreting current and upcoming spectroscopic surveys requires mock catalogues spanning Gpc-scale volumes while capturing small-scale intergalactic medium physics. This combination of high resolution and large volume is prohibitively expensive for hydrodynamical simulations. We present a field-level emulator, based on a three-dimensional U-Net, that maps approximate density and velocity fields directly to Ly$α$ optical depth and transmitted flux. At $z\sim3$, we train in small volumes and test on much larger, independent ones in two settings: IllustrisTNG (training on a $110\,\mathrm{cMpc}$ box and testing on a $300\,\mathrm{cMpc}$ box with 2LPT and $N$-body inputs) and FLAMINGO (training on $1\,\mathrm{cGpc}$ and testing on $2.8\,\mathrm{cGpc}$ with $N$-body inputs). The hydrodynamical statistics of TNG and FLAMINGO differ appreciably over their common $k$-range, by $\sim15\%$ in $P_{\rm 1D}$, $\sim17\%$ in the bispectrum, and $\sim40\%$ in the connected trispectrum, although their normalized power-spectrum correlation structures remain broadly similar. Within each suite, the emulator reproduces $P_{\rm 1D}$ to $2.8\%$ in TNG and $5.6\%$ in FLAMINGO, the bispectrum to $4$--$5\%$, and the trispectrum to $10$--$16\%$, while also recovering the flux PDF and broad correlation structure. Field-level emulation thus provides a practical route to large-volume Ly$α$-forest mocks for current and future surveys.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables, submitted to JCAP. Comments are welcome

papers.t: The relation between DCN/DNC ratios and gas temperature in late-stage massive star-forming regions using Yebes observations
papers.abs: Deuterated molecules probe the physical and chemical evolution of molecular clouds and star-forming regions. Their abundances depend on temperature, density, and evolutionary stage. DCN and DNC are relatively abundant deuterated isomers that probe temperature-dependent deuterium chemistry. Although [HCN]/[HNC] is often thought to increase in warmer gas, the temperature dependence of [DCN]/[DNC] remains less well constrained. To investigate how [DCN]/[DNC] depends on the gas kinetic temperature, we observed the $J$=1-0 transitions of DCN, DNC, H$^{13}$CN, HN$^{13}$C, HC$^{15}$N, and H$^{15}$NC toward 101 late-stage massive star-forming regions using the Yebes 40m telescope. Gas kinetic temperatures were estimated from CH$_3$CCH 5-4, whose rotation temperature is closely related to the kinetic temperature of dense gas. These temperatures were adopted in the column density calculations and in the analysis of temperature-dependent abundance ratios. We find a moderate positive correlation between the abundance ratio [DCN]/[DNC] and kinetic temperature, which is statistically significant and indicates that DCN becomes progressively more abundant relative to DNC in warmer gas. A weak negative correlation with temperature is observed for $D_{\rm frac}({\rm HNC})$, whereas no statistically significant correlation is found for $D_{\rm frac}({\rm HCN})$. The [HCN]/[HNC] ratios show substantial scatter and no statistically significant correlation with temperature, possibly due in part to optical-depth effects in the $^{13}$C isotopologues and the limited sensitivity of the $^{15}$N isotopologue observations. These results suggest that [DCN]/[DNC] may be governed not only by HCN/HNC isomeric chemistry but also by temperature-dependent deuterium fractionation pathways and the chemical evolution of dense gas.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in A&A, 28 pages, 13 figures

papers.t: IGRINS-2 Reveals an Oxygen-rich Dayside Atmosphere of WASP-12 b: Resolving the C/O Controversy
papers.abs: Recent studies have shown that measurements of hot-Jupiter atmospheric composition, including carbon-to-oxygen (C/O) and refractory-to-volatile (R/V) abundance ratios, provide powerful diagnostics of the chemistry and formation of gas giant planets. Important questions remain about the atmospheric composition of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b: its dayside C/O ratio remains under debate, and its R/V ratio is not yet well constrained. We present high-resolution (R $\sim$ 45,000) near-infrared dayside emission spectroscopy of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b with IGRINS-2 on Gemini North during post-eclipse phases. Cross-correlation analysis reveals volatile molecular signals of H$_2$O and CO together with tentative signals of OH and gas-phase refractories in the planetary atmosphere. The planetary signals appear in emission, indicating a thermal inversion in the dayside atmosphere. A chemically consistent Bayesian retrieval yields C/O $=0.72^{+0.08}_{-0.10}$, disfavoring carbon-rich dayside solutions with C/O $>1$ at greater than $5σ$. This independent, line-resolved measurement supports an oxygen-rich atmosphere, providing a new constraint on the long-standing C/O controversy surrounding WASP-12 b. Our retrieval also yields a host-star-normalized R/V ratio, $[\mathrm{R/V}]_{*}=0.17^{+0.22}_{-0.23}$, which is consistent with those of other ultra-hot Jupiters similarly characterized with IGRINS/IGRINS-2. Although the sample remains small, this consistency suggests a shared atmospheric chemistry among these planets, potentially reflecting similar proportions of accreted volatile and refractory material.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in ApJL

papers.t: Ultraviolet Observations of Solar Active Phenomena
papers.abs: Ultraviolet observations of the Sun have revolutionized our understanding of the structure and dynamics of the solar atmosphere. From the chromosphere all the way to the corona, there are ubiquitous jets due to magnetic reconnection and associated with type III radio bursts. Sporadic flares occur in the corona, representing an inevitable breakup of magnetic energy accumulation as new magnetic flux continues to pump into the solar atmosphere, which is further shuffled by solar surface motions. Once large-scale eruptions occur, magnetized plasmas are expelled out into the interplanetary space, leaving globally propagating waves and the following dimmings. The waves can be utilized to diagnose the coronal magnetic field which cannot be measured directly, and the dimmings can be used to estimate the ejected mass of eruptions and magnetic connectivity. Extreme ultraviolet spectroscopic observations provide information on the fractionation of different chemical elements, in particular those elements with low first ionization potential. Thanks to the high spatial resolution of solar observations, all these results are believed to shed light on our understanding of the activity on other stars which cannot be imaged.
papers.comment: 71 pages, 12 figures, accepted for publication in Space Sci. Rev

papers.t: Beyond the Peak: Constraining early dark energy with the damping tail
papers.abs: Early dark energy is commonly characterized by the amplitude and location of its primary energy-injection peak. We show that its post-peak evolution, which we call the \emph{EDE tail}, provides an additional observable probe of the underlying scalar dynamics and can materially affect its ability to alleviate the Hubble tension. We construct a simple phenomenological framework in which distinct regions of a multiscale scalar potential govern the dynamics at different field scales. As a representative realization, we consider a potential that combines axion-like and $α$-attractor-like regimes, thereby allowing the EDE tail to be reshaped through reflection and asymmetric oscillations. Confronting this framework with cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation, and supernova observations, we find an improved fit to the high-$\ell$ CMB data together with a higher inferred bestfit $H_0$. Our results show that the EDE tail retains observable information about the underlying scalar potential that is not captured by the conventional peak parameters alone. This provides a complementary route for constructing and observationally distinguishing EDE scenarios, and potentially for further alleviating the Hubble tension.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 8 figures

papers.t: Disentangling Disk and Broad-Line Region Continuum Emission in a Sample of Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.abs: Recent continuum reverberation-mapping measurements of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) indicate that the inter-band time lags are significantly larger than those predicted by the light travel times across the standard thin model. In addition, the observed $u$-band excess suggests the presence of diffuse continuum (DC) radiation originating in the broad-line region (BLR). Spectroscopically, the Balmer and Paschen jumps in DC emission are unique indicators to quantify the contributions of the BLR to the observed continuum. Here, we study the DC contributions of 31 AGNs, whose spectra are obtained with the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS) on the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and with X-shooter on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). In each spectrum, at least one of the Balmer and Paschen jumps is covered. For each object, we performed radiative transfer calculations using Cloudy within the Locally Optimally-emitting Clouds (LOC) model to construct source-specific DC spectral templates. We quantified the DC contribution by incorporating these templates as continuum components in spectral decomposition. The average ratio of the DC to total (i.e., disk+DC) continua is ~33% just below the Balmer jump (~3625 Å). The Balmer jump provides a stronger constraint on the DC component than the Paschen jump. Simulations based on mock spectra further demonstrate that an unsuitable template can introduce systematic, wavelength-dependent biases to the inferred DC fraction. Our results underscore the importance of employing appropriate DC templates in the spectral decomposition to infer the substantial DC contribution. Upcoming time-resolved spectra will enable more detailed modelling and tighter constraints on the disk and BLR.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables; the decomposition results and the DC templates can be downloaded from https://doi.org/10.12149/101886

papers.t: Precise Radii of Visual Binaries with Dynamical Masses: ξ Bootis & 70 Ophiuchi
papers.abs: A new orbital solution for $ξ$ Bootis (GJ 566 AB, P=152 yrs) and the recently revised orbital solution for 70 Ophiuchi (GJ 702 AB, P=88 yrs) yield component masses precise to 0.4\%. Their relatively wide separations ($>0.4^{\prime\prime}$) allow the components to be studied independently, making them ideal for testing the predictions of stellar evolutionary models. We use the six-telescope near-infrared MIRC-X and MYSTIC beam combiners at the CHARA Array to measure the angular diameters of all 4 stars. Combined with precise Gaia DR3 parallax values and bolometric fluxes, these interferometric measurements translate to stellar radii that are precise to $<2.4\%$ and effective temperatures precise to $<1.7\%$. We compare the measured radii and temperatures to four stellar evolutionary models (Lyon, Dartmouth, PARSEC, MIST). Over the mass range $0.67 - 0.91$ M$_\odot$, all models reproduce the observed properties within a few standard deviations, with no systematic offsets. The pairs are coeval and consistent with independent age estimates, further validating model predictions. With physical separations greater than 20 au, these pairs show no evidence of radius inflation, despite being spectroscopically classified as chromospherically active, and in the case of $ξ$ Bootis, probable members of the adolescent age ($\sim 0.4$ Gyr) Ursa Majoris Moving Group. In contrast, a set of 21 short-period ($P\lesssim$ 10 days) eclipsing binary stars with similar dynamical masses and metallicities are larger and often cooler than these same model predictions. Within this mass range, radius inflation appears to be associated with short-period binary star systems.
papers.comment: 26 pages, 13 figures, accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal

papers.t: Computing the Wave: Bridging Gravitational Wave and High-Energy-Physics software (with modular ROOT extensions)
papers.abs: High-Energy Physics (HEP) and Gravitational Wave (GW) astronomy pursue different scientific goals, yet they face strikingly similar computing challenges and can enrich one another through shared software. Building on the prototype presented at ACAT 2024, we report on the consolidation of that work into a single, modular extension of the CERN ROOT data-analysis framework, freely distributed under RIOPlus. The library is now organised as a set of optional, dynamically loadable extensions covering configuration and file-format parsing (including the Gravitational Wave Frame (GWF) format and HDF5), remote and federated data access (OSDF/Pelican, S3, Kafka) with token-based credentials, an enhanced dynamic-display manager, an advanced signal-processing layer built on the KFR library, and a complex-capable tensor layer backed by LibTorch with ONNX interoperability. We summarise the design of each extension, outline the intended application to transient-noise (glitch) detection and classification, and update the FFT performance benchmark comparing KFR with FFTW. We close with the end-to-end ROOT-centred workflow these extensions enable, its current status, and an outlook toward column-wise RNTuple storage.

papers.t: Physics-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement of Amortized Bayesian Inference Across Physics
papers.abs: Across physics, from the orbits of imaged exoplanets and the matter inside neutron stars to thin films at synchrotrons and cortical neurons, conservation laws, interference, and compensating currents compress the posteriors of precise data into tiny, curved regions where Markov chains need minutes to days. We introduce PhyRSI (physics-guided recursive self-improvement), in which an AI agent coupled to the simulator writes and revises an amortized Bayesian inference algorithm for each field, scored by the importance weights of the exact likelihood because the true posterior is unknown.
